day_shape: 69 items: CENTCOM disables Bandar Abbas-origin M/V Pacific Archer in Gulf of Oman after blockade-run, IRGC reports two tanker explosions near Strait of Hormuz, Israeli strike targets Khalil al-Hayya's son in Gaza, Iran International reports Iraq shuts two more border crossings; nothing from UK Parliament or IAEA.

threads.label: US blockade enforcement in Gulf of Oman
threads.summary: CENTCOM said it disabled Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on 26 November with precision munitions after the vessel left Bandar Abbas and tried to run the US naval blockade. Iran International and Jerusalem Post reported it as the first disabling since Iranian adviser Mohammad Mokhber vowed to break the blockade.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions and Navy rhetoric
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press said the IRGC Navy reported two smuggled tankers exploded near Khassab port and east of the Strait of Hormuz, one hit by a sea mine, and UKMTO logged a Sea of Oman security incident. The Army Navy commander claimed revenge for the Dena martyrs and warned shipowners against US 'deception', calling the blockade meaningless.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and al-Hayya son targeted
threads.summary: Israeli reporting and Hamas-linked statements said an overnight strike on Gaza City's Rimal neighbourhood targeted Izz al-Hayya, youngest son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, wounding six including his wife. The IDF also reported killing 10 Hamas and PIJ operatives over the week and bombing four weapon depots.

threads.label: Basij anniversary messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office and IRIB pushed Basij anniversary content praising faith and 'harshness against disbelievers', with messages from Hezbollah's Naim Qassem and commanders Quraishi and Hasanzadeh. Defa Press also relayed Minister of Defence Akhlaq and Khamenei adviser messages tying Basij to the 'third imposed war'.

threads.label: Iran economic and domestic pressure
threads.summary: Iran International reported central bank governor acknowledging limited FX access and the unofficial dollar above 2.93 million rials, and a top psychiatrist's warning that bootleg alcohol poisonings have killed at least 26 and sickened over 550. It also reported hardliner criticism of Pezeshkian's unheated-office austerity gesture.

threads.label: External pressure on Iran in Europe and Iraq
threads.summary: Iran International reported Iraq shut two more border crossings with Iran this week following a US request to keep only two open, and cited an IISS report finding Iran has sustained European operations at up to 12 incidents a month. Sweden Democrats also filed a motion to sanction Iranian officials' families and expel suspected spies.

threads.label: Israeli coalition politics and UNIFIL
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas is expected to declare Hamas a terrorist organisation in a Channel 12 interview amid coalition talks, with Ben-Gvir accusing him of lying. Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam said a French proposal could extend UNIFIL beyond its 31 December mandate, and Danny Danon demanded an apology from UN aid chief Tom Fletcher.

events.title_en: Germany approves unprecedented 610 billion dollar budget
events.summary_en: Germany approves unprecedented 610 billion dollar budget. The German parliament approved an unprecedented 610 billion dollar budget for the country for 2027. This budget includes a significant increase in defence expenditure and a reduction in foreign aid and Germany's contribution to the United Nations. According to the approved budget, Germany's defence expenditure in 2027 will reach approximately 153 billion dollars, showing an increase of approximately 34 billion dollars compared to last year. In contrast, Germany's development budget and foreign aid will decrease by approximately 4.7 per cent, falling from 10.06 billion euros in 2026 to 9.58 billion euros in 2027.
